results.question: What are the key compliance deadlines for merchant bankers under the January 2026 SEBI amendment?
results.ground_truth: The SEBI circular (January 2, 2026) on Merchant Bankers Regulations amendments has the following deadlines: (1) By February 2, 2026 — disclose non-SEBI regulated activities on website. (2) By April 3, 2026 — ensure compliance officer independence, close outsourced core merchant banking activities. (3) By July 3, 2026 — segregate non-SEBI regulated activities into separate business units with Chinese Wall, submit compliance report for non-SEBI regulated activities. (4) By January 2, 2027 — submit CA certified net worth certificate for categorization, ensure NISM certifications for employees, ensure principal officer has 5 years experience. (5) By January 2, 2028 — comply with underwriting obligations not exceeding 20 times liquid net worth. (6) First assessment from April 1, 2029 — minimum revenue generation requirements (Rs. 25 crore for Category I, Rs. 5 crore for Category II cumulative over three preceding financial years).

results.question: As a Tier 4 Urban Cooperative Bank, can we provide working capital loans secured by gold to a jewellery manufacturer?
results.ground_truth: Yes, with conditions. Under the RBI's amended Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral Directions (1st Amendment, September 29, 2025, circular RBI/2025-26/84), Scheduled Commercial Banks and Tier 3 or 4 UCBs may extend need-based working capital finance to borrowers using gold or silver as raw material or input in manufacturing or industrial processing. However, borrowers must not acquire or hold gold for investment or speculative purposes. Separately, lenders shall not grant advances for the purchase of gold in any form (primary gold, ornaments, jewellery, coins, ETFs, Mutual Funds) or against primary gold/silver or financial assets backed by primary gold/silver.

*   **Valuation:** Gold jewellery accepted as security/collateral must be valued at the average of the closing price of 22 carat gold for the preceding 30 days as quoted by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd. (RBI/2022-23/22). UCBs may also use the historical spot gold price data of the preceding 30 days publicly disseminated by a Commodity Exchange regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (RBI/2022-23/22, RBI/2025-26/18). If the gold is of purity less than 22 carats, the UCB should translate the collateral into 22 carat and value the exact grams of the collateral (RBI/2022-23/22, RBI/2025-26/18).
*   **Safeguards:** UCBs are advised to observe the safeguards detailed in Annex-3 to mitigate the risks attached to loans and advances against gold/silver ornaments (RBI/2025-26/18).
*   **Bullet Repayment:** The amount of loan sanctioned should not exceed ₹2.00 lakh at any point of time and the period of the loan shall not exceed 12 months from the date of sanction (RBI/2023-24/51). Banks should maintain a Loan to Value (LTV) ratio of 75% on the outstanding amount of loan including the interest on an ongoing basis, failing which the loan will be treated as Non Performing Asset (NPA) (RBI/2023-24/51).
*   **Credit Policy:** The credit policy of a bank shall include, inter alia, appropriate single borrower limits and aggregate limits for the portfolio of loans against collateral of jewellery, ornaments or coins made of gold or silver; maximum LTV ratio permissible for such loans; action to be taken in cases of breach of LTV ratio; valuation standards and norms; and standards of gold and silver purity (RBI/DOR/2025-26/229).

results.question: What specific changes were made to the NCS Master Circular for green debt security reviewer appointments?
results.ground_truth: Per SEBI circular dated February 27, 2026 (ref: HO/17/11/24(1)2026-DDHS-POD1/I/5967/2026), Chapter IX Paragraph 1.8 of the NCS Master Circular was deleted and a new Paragraph 5 was inserted. The changes align the requirements for appointing an independent third-party reviewer/certifier for green debt securities with those for social and sustainability bonds. The reviewer must be independent of the issuer and have expertise in ESG debt securities. The scope of the review and details of the reviewer must be disclosed in the offer document. The circular applies to issuers of green debt securities, recognized stock exchanges, recognized depositories, registered merchant bankers, registered debenture trustees, registered credit rating agencies, and registered ESG ratings providers.

*   **Deletion of Paragraph 1.8:** Paragraph 1.8 of Chapter IX of the NCS Master Circular has been deleted (SEBI Circular No: HO/17/11/24(1)2026-DDHS-POD1/I/5967/2026).
*   **Insertion of Paragraph 5:** The following paragraph has been inserted as "paragraph 5" in Chapter IX of the NCS Master Circular (SEBI Circular No: HO/17/11/24(1)2026-DDHS-POD1/I/5967/2026):
